# CBAM compliance answer, v1

You answer questions about the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
using only the retrieved context below. You are read by compliance staff who
will act on what you write, so an admission of missing information is more
useful than a plausible guess.

## Rules

1. Use only the context. Do not use background knowledge about CBAM, EU law or
   emissions trading, even if you are confident it is correct.
2. Cite every factual claim with the chunk id it came from, in square
   brackets, exactly as the id appears in the context: `[reg_2023_956#0007]`.
   A sentence may carry more than one citation.
3. If the context does not contain enough to answer, say exactly what is
   missing and stop. Do not answer partially and then hedge.
4. Quote the operative wording of an obligation (deadline, threshold, duty
   holder) rather than paraphrasing it.
5. No preamble, no restatement of the question, no closing summary. Answer in
   at most 200 words.

Synthetic guidance for installation operators outside the customs territory

1 Why you are being asked for data
An importer in the customs territory has to report the emissions embedded in the
goods it buys from you. It cannot do that without data from the installation
where the goods were made. You are not directly subject to the synthetic
Regulation, and no penalty under it applies to you, but the importer's ability
to keep buying from you depends on the data you provide.

2 What an installation is
A stationary technical unit where a production process is carried out. If your
site runs several production processes, each is reported separately, with its
own activity level and its own attributed emissions.

coordinates of the main emission source, and the United Nations code for trade
and transport locations for the site. These identify the installation across

Article 9
Correction procedure initiated by the competent authority
Where the competent authority finds that a CBAM report is incomplete or
incorrect, it shall communicate the assessment to the reporting declarant and
request the declarant to submit a corrected report. The declarant shall be given
a period of no less than 15 and no more than 30 calendar days to submit the
corrected report.

Article 10
Penalties

3 What changes and when
From 1 October 2023 to 31 December 2025 you only report. You do not buy

4 Quarterly reporting during the transitional period
You submit one report per quarter through the transitional registry, within one
month of the quarter ending. So the report for January to March is due by 30

production route was used, and the emissions embedded in it, split into direct
and indirect. You also report any carbon price you already paid in the country
where the goods were made.

Synthetic Regulation on a carbon border adjustment mechanism

CHAPTER I
Subject matter, scope and definitions

Article 1
Subject matter
This synthetic Regulation establishes a carbon border adjustment mechanism for
addressing embedded emissions in the goods listed in Annex I on their
importation into the customs territory, with a view to preventing the risk of
carbon leakage and thereby reducing global carbon emissions. The mechanism
applies in parallel with the emissions trading system and is designed so that
imported goods bear a carbon price equivalent to the price borne by goods
produced within the customs territory.

Article 2
Scope
This Regulation applies to goods listed in Annex I originating in a third
country, where those goods, or processed products from those goods resulting
from the inward processing procedure, are imported into the customs territory.
It does not apply to goods whose total intrinsic value, per consignment, does
not exceed EUR 150. It does not apply to

[syn_guidance_importers#0005] (SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT - NOT LAW. Written for the evalgate test harness. It is not)
the country of origin for the same emissions. You have to have actually
paid it, and there must not have been a rebate or other compensation on export.
Keep documentation, certified by an independent person.

11 Penalties during the transitional period
If you do not report, or you report something incomplete or incorrect and do not
fix it when asked, the penalty is between EUR 10 and EUR 50 per tonne of
unreported emissions. It goes up if you have submitted more than two bad reports
in a row or if you have not reported for more than six months. The authority
takes into account how much was missing, whether you cooperated, and whether it
was deliberate.

12 Common mistakes
Reporting electricity in tonnes rather than megawatt hours. Assuming the
estimated values published for the transitional period remain available after 31
July 2024. Assuming indirect emissions are reported for iron and steel during
the transitional period, when only direct emissions are. Forgetting that the
EUR 150 threshold is per consignment, not per year.

Synthetic guidance for importers of goods covered by the mechanism

1 Purpose of this guidance
This guidance explains in plain language what an importer has to do under the
synthetic Regulation and the synthetic Implementing Regulation. Where this
guidance and those documents differ, the documents govern. It is written for
people who import goods and who are not lawyers.

2 Do the rules apply to me
They apply if you import cement, electricity, fertilisers, iron and steel,
aluminium or hydrogen into the customs territory. They do not apply if the total
value of a consignment is EUR 150 or less. They do not apply to goods you carry
in personal baggage below that value, or to goods for military use. If you buy
covered goods from a supplier inside the customs territory, you are not the
importer and the reporting obligation is not yours.

9 Carbon prices you already pay
If your emissions are subject to a carbon price where you are, tell the importer
the price due for the emissions concerned and whether any rebate or other
compensation is available on export. The importer can only claim a reduction
where the price was effectively paid and no export rebate was available.

10 What happens if you provide nothing
The importer records the request and the absence of a response, and falls back
to default values. Default values are set at the average emission intensity of
your country for that type of goods, increased by a mark-up. If reliable country
data is not available, they are based on the average of the ten worst performing
installations in the customs territory. Both are usually worse for you than your
actual figures.
